author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. A successful correction updates that visit in place, adds no visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record; a refused one shows the form again.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit is updated, no visit is added, and the owner's record is shown.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named.
[REQ-VIS-003] Visits edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or that belongs to a different pet, is refused rather than showing an empty form.
[REQ-VIS-003] Visits edge case 4: a visit dated today or earlier cannot keep its date through a correction; changing only its description is refused.
non_goals: Any link or other visible entry point to the correction, on the owner detail page or elsewhere (owner decision, intake line 1; a follow-up request may add one).
New wording for the correction: heading, submit label, or confirmation message. The reused form keeps its booking wording (open question in docs/prd.md).
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner.
notes: Mechanism fixed by the owner's request (intake line 1), for system-design: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the existing form template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with its `visit` model attribute prefilled; POST to the same URL validates like creation (description required, date after today), updates the visit in place, and redirects to the owner detail page; on validation failure it redisplays the form. Test names: the nonexistent-visit and other-pet cases of edge case 3 are one data-driven test. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: past-dated visits (narrowest reading = edge case 4) and entry point/wording (deferred). Outside this dispatch's write scope, for system-design-expert/doc-sync: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for docs/adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; docs/system-design.md VisitController row should cite REQ-VIS-003. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction follows the existing edit seam PetController already demonstrates: a per-request @ModelAttribute that loads the existing entity when an optional path id is present and builds a new one otherwise, with the write going through OwnerRepository by cascade (system-design § Contracts, invariants paragraph: Owner is the aggregate entry point, no Visit repository). The adjustment: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId path variable. With visitId it resolves the visit through Pet (new lookup on Pet, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)) and appends no new visit. Without it, booking is unchanged. Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm is reused unchanged: it posts to the current URL, shows the 'New' heading only for an unsaved visit, and lists persisted visits. Basis: grep and read of VisitController, PetController.findPet, Owner.getPet, Pet.addVisit and the template (IDE oracle not connected, so the weaker basis). Design-doc writes: Contracts rows for Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now cite REQ-VIS-003; an invariant records that a visit is reached only through its pet; the Threat Model mass-assignment row and a new derived Known Defects row record a pre-existing owner-binding exposure (see notes); docs/adr/README.md index gains the 2026-09-11 non-goal ADR row the prd-entry flagged.
integration_points: Entry point GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, binding target: the persisted Visit resolved from the path pet's own visits, behind an allow-list of date and description (an @InitBinder("visit") setAllowedFields). The controller-wide id / *.id disallow list stays, per security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row.
Owner model attribute on the correction POST: the handler takes it with binding disabled (@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)). The owner is the save target, never a binding target.

Pet gains a lookup of one of its persisted visits by identity, returning null when absent and skipping unsaved visits (the Owner.getPet(Integer) convention). Unit-testable on real Pet and Visit objects with no double.

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository) in VisitControllerTests: reuse the class's existing @MockitoBean stub. This is a conscious exception under testing-principles § Mocking Policy: the @WebMvcTest slice carries no persistence, a hand-written double would implement the whole JpaRepository surface, and the class already carries the stub. For the in-place-update test, seed the stubbed owner's pet with one persisted visit, then assert on that same owner graph after the POST: the pet still holds exactly one visit, carrying the submitted values. Also verify that save was called.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned double (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).
Success redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. Validation failure returns pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with field errors on visit.

patterns.description: findPet: optional path id in a @ModelAttribute method, existing entity when present, new entity when absent. The shape for loadPetWithVisit.
getPet(Integer): identity lookup that skips unsaved children and returns null. The shape for the new Pet visit lookup.
The existing non-future-date check and its typeMismatch.visitDate code. Extract it to one private method called by both booking and correction.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit runs before every handler and appends a new unsaved Visit to the pet. Left on the correction path, save cascades an extra visit (or fails bean validation on persist), which breaks 'no visit is added'.
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId so the correction path appends nothing (system-design § Contracts invariants: Pet and Visit persist only by cascade from Owner). The in-place-update test asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged.

risks.risk: Mass assignment onto the owner: a bound Owner parameter on the correction POST would let any submitted owner field overwrite and persist owner details, as booking and the pet forms do today.
risks.mitigation: Disable owner binding and allow-list the visit binder (security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row; system-design § Known Defects, owner-binding row).

risks.risk: Adding a date check to the new handler would be a fresh controller rule (architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Web controller row and the note after it).
risks.mitigation: Correction reuses booking's single non-future-date check through one shared private method, with no second copy and no new rule. Moving the rule out of the controller stays Open Question 2 in system-design and is not this slice's call.

risks.risk: A visitId that does not exist or belongs to another pet could show an empty form, or correct another pet's visit.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only through the path's pet (aggregates entered through the root, architecture-principles closed kernel). On a miss, refuse with the same IllegalArgumentException convention loadPetWithVisit already uses for a missing owner or pet. The message carries identifiers only, since the error page renders it (security-principles § Realization, secret-disclosure row).

risks.risk: A POST trusting the visit resolved by the earlier GET.
risks.mitigation: The per-request @ModelAttribute re-resolves owner, pet and visit from the path on every request; nothing goes into session (security-principles § Realization, cross-request-state row).

risks.risk: A validation failure leaving a half-applied write.
risks.mitigation: Binding mutates the detached visit in memory only; on errors the handler returns the form before save (architecture-principles § Design Principles, fail secure).

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. No ADR: the slice reuses the PetController edit pattern, so no trade-off constrains later slices. Edge case 4 (a past-dated visit cannot keep its date) falls out of the shared booking check with no extra code. Correction adds no confirmation flash message: the prd-entry declines new confirmation wording, and reusing 'Your visit has been booked' would misstate the action. The PRD Open Questions already defer this wording. Pre-existing exposure surfaced for the human, derived from code and unconfirmed: PetController create/edit and VisitController booking take the loaded Owner as a bound model attribute whose binder disallows only id, so a submitted owner field (for example lastName) is bound and saved. It is recorded in system-design § Known Defects and qualified in the Threat Model. This slice does not fix it (outside REQ-VIS-003 scope), and the correction does not repeat it. The uncommitted non-goal ADR edits (2026-08-08 status line, new 2026-09-11 file) are product-requirements-expert's writes and are not claimed here.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: An empty date slips past validation on the new correction path and wipes the date stored on a booked visit. The check is `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()))`, so it skips a null date. Visit.date carries no @NotNull (Visit.java:38-40 has `@Column(name = "visit_date")`, `@DateTimeFormat(pattern = "yyyy-MM-dd")`, `private LocalDate date;`). The column is nullable (h2/schema.sql:61 `visit_date  DATE,`, same in mysql and postgres). The form has no client-side guard either: `grep -F 'required' templates/fragments/inputField.html` returned nothing. Attack path: POST /owners/{o}/pets/{p}/visits/{v}/edit with `date=&description=x`. Spring's formatting conversion turns empty text into null, which I reasoned from the framework and did not execute in this review. Validation then passes, and owners.save(owner) cascades a null visit_date onto an existing visit. This breaks the trust-boundary rule 'reject what the contract does not allow': REQ-VIS-003 corrects a visit 'under the same rules as booking', and REQ-VIS-001 records a visit only when 'a date later than today' is supplied. The weakness already exists: booking (processNewVisitForm) shares the same helper and accepts an empty date the same way. The correction path widens it from creating a dateless visit to destroying valid stored data, which sets the severity: data integrity, no confidentiality or privilege impact.
findings.fix: In rejectDateNotAfterToday, reject a null date before the ordering check, e.g. `if (visit.getDate() == null) { result.rejectValue("date", "required"); } else if (!visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())) { result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate"); }`. The key exists: messages.properties:2 `required=is required`. Add a correction test submitting `date=` that asserts a field error on `date` and no save. Because the helper is shared, booking is covered by the same fix.

approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the new `@InitBinder("visit")` sets `setAllowedFields("date", "description")` (VisitController.java:58-61), on top of the unqualified `@InitBinder` `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (VisitController.java:53-56). The correction handler takes `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) Owner owner`, so no submitted owner field reaches the saved aggregate. The allow-list also narrows the booking binder, so the control got stronger, not weaker.

Ownership and cross-request state: every request re-resolves the visit through owner, then pet, then `pet.getVisit(visitId)` (VisitController.java:84-91). Pet.getVisit only matches persisted visits held by that pet (Pet.java `if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`). A foreign or unknown visit id is refused before any binding, and VisitControllerTests covers both GET and POST for those ids.

Error output: the new IllegalArgumentException message holds only the caller-supplied integers visitId and petId, so no sensitive value reaches the error page (whose message rendering is a recorded Known Defect).

XSS: the reused template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit data only through th:text and th:field via the inputField fragment. No unescaped output (th:utext) is added. The form has no th:action, so a correction posts back to its own /edit URL.

Injection and surface: the change adds no query text, file or resource path, shell call, deserialization entry point, logging, or secret; production changes are limited to Pet.java and VisitController.java per `scripts/changeset.sh --name-only`. The new GET/POST /edit routes fall within the recorded no-auth/no-CSRF demonstration baseline (security-principles.md § What this application is), and the GET handler takes no bound parameter, so it cannot mutate state.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set. `grep -i 'dependencycheck|owasp' build.gradle` found no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin, so no NVD match ran. Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1 (spring-boot-thymeleaf), spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson), thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final. I did not re-run `./gradlew test` in this review; I rely on the build-pass gate.

author: change-grader
summary: add correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Contained to one package: a 15-line identity lookup on Pet, the VisitController edit routes, their tests, and docs recording the NG-5 narrowing; no sensitive paths, and the new unauthenticated write route sits inside the recorded no-auth demonstration baseline.

semantic_surprise.note: The shared rejectDateNotAfterToday helper (VisitController.java:147) now refuses a null date with 'required', which silently changes the existing booking flow as well: an empty-date booking that used to save a dateless visit is now refused. Separately, correction follows booking's future-date rule, so a past visit's description cannot be fixed without moving its date forward; this is deliberate, tested, and recorded as a PRD open question, but the owner has to accept it.

test_adequacy.note: The correction tests are real. They assert the same visit instance is updated with no second visit, no save on any refusal, foreign and unknown visit ids refused on GET and POST, and owner fields unchanged under tampering. The booking path's new empty-date refusal has no booking test and is pinned only indirectly through the helper's correction test, and cascade persistence is proven only against a mocked OwnerRepository.

reviewer_hedging.note: The final roster is unanimous, but the security reviewer's round-1 changes_requested (bar_clause secure-by-design: an empty date wiped a stored visit_date) was reworked before approval. The round-2 citations resolve exactly (VisitController.java:115/137 helper calls before :122/:143 saves). The missing dependency scanner is a standing project gap, and the code-quality recommendation concerns pre-existing style.

scope_deviation.note: Stays on the intake's surface: GET/POST edit routes, form reuse, validation parity, no owner-page link, and the NG-5 narrowing recorded as a non-goal ADR. There were zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries. The booking-path null-date change follows REQ-VIS-001's existing 'date later than today' rule rather than adding new scope.
